correctness.rationale: Global exclusion: the difference equation (T-2)delta=T M eta and strict monotonicity force T>2 by positive symmetric quadratic form. Existence: explicit full box stays in opposite quadrants, fixed-point map moves each coordinate at most (27/5)E and contracts with Lipschitz <=216 exp(-6)<1 for alpha>=10. Differentiating F proves uniform complex-vector expansion >=1+(T-2)(1-108 exp(-6))>1 at both members. These analytic inequalities prove all quantifiers; the packaged program independently checks 21 high-precision examples and numerical residuals.

originality.rationale: The full open-access defining article was read for the precise map and relevant bifurcation sections. It does not prove the sharp global primitive-two exclusion at step 2 or construct a saturated hyperbolic repeller for all larger steps and alpha>=10. Closest indexed analogues use inequivalent Rulkov, Duffing and Tinkerbell maps; those theorems cannot imply the present statement without an unreported conjugacy. General monotonicity and contraction methods are not claimed original. Remaining priority uncertainty is explicitly noted.
residual_risks: The existence of an unindexed, unpublished or otherwise inaccessible equivalent calculation is not ruled out.
Related index records for other maps were reviewed through their published summaries, not by opening each full article; their different equations make them lower-priority material comparisons.

value.rationale: A sharp global obstruction at the time-discretization frontier, paired with an explicit repelling orbit above it, resolves whether primitive two-step dynamics is possible in a numerically studied neuron map. Repellers are not detected by ordinary forward attractor bifurcation plots. The explicit contraction box, exponential orbit bounds and uniform hyperbolicity are mathematically usable, non-routine dynamical information; no stronger global uniqueness is claimed.
